newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak yen boosts Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' profits.
newsitem.headline: Weak yen boosts Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' profits.

text.p: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd., Japan's largest machinery maker, said Thursday that sales and profits rose to record levels in the first half, bolstered by the weak yen.

The maker of products ranging from aircraft to air conditioners said current profits rose nearly 13 percent to 89.14 billion yen ($788 million) in the six months to Sept. 30, from 79.17 billion yen ($701 million) in the 1995 period.
Sales rose 10 percent to 1.18 trillion yen ($10.45 billion) from 1.07 trillion ($9.47 billion).
"We posted our largest-ever interim sales and profits. We received more yen for dollar-denominated exports due to the weaker yen," a company spokesman said.
Current profits are pre-tax and include gains and losses on investments and other non-operating activities. The yen's value against the dollar has dropped about 13 percent over the past year.
In the first half of the fiscal year, exports accounted for 30.9 percent of overall sales. In the same period a year ago, the ratio was 22.8 percent.

Mitsubishi Heavy also raised its half-year dividend for the first time since the 1990/91 business year, paying out five yen (four cents), up from the four yen (3.5 cents) it paid for the same period a year ago.
In the six-month period, the company saw higher sales at all its divisions except at industrial plants, general machinery and air conditioning systems, the spokesman said.

Sales at its aircraft and special vehicles divisions in the six-month period jumped 70 percent from the same period a year ago, partly because of sales of Boeing 777 aircraft, which Mitsubishi jointly developed and makes with Boeing Co., the spokesman said.
